title: Cap. IV Arg. 8 Sol: conclusion does not force foresight-election; Major mixes Decernere and Servare
pass_a_gloss: Solution. We say that the conclusion does not directly contradict our position. For what ought to have been concluded was, Therefore God elected to glory only the faithful, and as faithful, from foresight of this faith. But that conclusion, Therefore he decreed from eternity to save only the faithful, as such, puts faith as an antecedent condition as to the very external conferring of the decreed salvation; which we do not deny; but not as to the very internal decree of God destinating to salvation; which ought to have been proved. Let us come to the ventilation of the Major. I say that in it two words are mixed and joined in bad faith, of which one designates the very destination to salvation in the Divine mind; the other the leading through to salvation in external execution. For the word to Decree regards the eternal and intrinsic act of the Divine will; the word to Save regards the extrinsic and temporal effect.
pass_b_english: Sol. The conclusion does not directly contradict us. What they needed was: therefore God elected to glory only the faithful as faithful, from foresight of that faith. Their conclusion — he decreed from eternity to save only the faithful as such — makes faith an antecedent condition for the external conferring of decreed salvation (which we grant), not for God's internal destinating decree (which they needed to prove). On the Major: two words are mixed in bad faith — one names destination to salvation in the divine mind, the other leading to salvation in external execution. Decernere looks to the eternal intrinsic act of will; Servare to the extrinsic temporal effect.
source_text: Sol. Conclusionem dicimus non directe contradicere sententiae nostrae. Conclusum enim oportuit, Ergo Deus solos fideles, et qua fideles, ex praevisione hujus fidei elegit ad gloriam. Illa autem conclusio, Ergo solos fideles ab aeterno decrevit, qua tales servare, ponit fidem antecedaneam conditionem quoad ipsam externam collationem decretae salutis; quod nos non negamus; non autem quoad ipsum internum decretum Dei ad salutem destinantis; quod probatum oportuit. Ad Majoris ventilationem accedamus. Dico in illa commisceri, et mala fide copulari duo vocabula, quorum unum designat ipsam destinationem ad salutem in mente Divina; alterum perductionem ad salutem in exsecutione externa. Nam verbum Decernere respicit actum voluntatis Divinae aeternum et intrinsecum; verbum Servare respicit effectum extrinsecum et temporalem.
